title: Compactification and Online Condensation — scratchpad
content:
Goal: gather promising ideas for reducing working-context footprint for on-device/edge LLMs while preserving downstream QA/assistant accuracy. Focus is on techniques that are cheap to run (no heavy re-training), work incrementally as the session grows, and can be rolled into Redwood Private/edge stacks.

High-level taxonomy I'm sketching:
- Extractive condensation: choose salient spans/tokens from earlier context to keep; maintain mapping to original positions so we can rehydrate if needed. Cheap but brittle on paraphrase.
- Progressive summaries (hierarchical): repeatedly compress groups of turns into short summaries, retaining anchors (named entities/time stamps) for quick retrieval. More robust but summary drift risk.
- Dense condensation (vectorized): compute embeddings for chunks and keep cluster centroids as compact proxies; need careful similarity thresholds and cheap recompute.
- Eviction policies + ephemeral context: time-decay / LRU for older tokens; baseline for everything else.
- Prompt rewriting / compaction at generation time: fold earlier turns into fewer exemplar prompts (few-shot style) that preserve instruction and constraints.

Notes on papers & posts I skimmed (quick takeaways + possible followups):
1) "Fast Condensing for Sequence Models" (arXiv 2028) — method: lightweight extractor network trained on teacher distillation to select 5–15% of tokens per 1k tokens. Pros: small runtime overhead, plug-in to KV-cache pipeline. Cons: needs training data representative of sessions.
   - Idea: try zero-shot heuristics (entity+topic change detection) first, then add small distillation when we have customer logs.

2) "EdgeLM: Tiny RAG for mobile" (industry blog, 2029 Q1) — RAG with compressed memories using Bloom-filter style signatures for quick candidate shortlist; rehydrate only top-k with full chunks.
   - Good for retrieval-heavy apps. Need to measure false-negative rate on short-term queries.

3) "Progressive Summaries" (workshop paper) — rollout-friendly: summarize every N turns with temperature-controlled model, store provenance. They recommend keeping both summary and 1–2 anchor utterances per block.
   - Practical: store (summary, anchor-ids) pairs in KV cache; allows quick expansion. Concern: how to enforce freshness without explosion of anchors.

4) "Contrastive Prompt Compaction" (ICLR submission 2029) — learns a compact pseudo-prompt vector representing prior turns, trained with contrastive objective to preserve next-token distributions. Requires additional model head.
   - Likely heavier to integrate into hosted API; might fit Dedicated with custom kernels. Worth prototyping as a research spike.

Implementation experiments to run (cheap to expensive):
- A) Heuristic entity-anchor compaction (cheap): extract named entities + last user instruction per 200 tokens, drop others. Run offline eval on sample session logs for recall@k of factual Q/A.
- B) Progressive block summarization with anchor retention: summarize every 6 turns using hosted small model (gpt-compact-1) with 60–120 token summaries + keep 1 anchor utterance. Measure latency and summary drift over 20-turn sessions.
- C) Embedding centroid condense: chunk 128-token blocks, compute embeddings, keep centroids + top exemplars per centroid. Evaluate on retrieval latency and end-task accuracy.
- D) Lightweight extractor distillation (harder): train a tiny selector model using teacher signals from full LLM to pick spans that preserve log-prob distribution on next tokens.

Metrics I care about:
- Task retention: delta in end-task metrics (QA F1 / dialogue success) relative to full context.
- Latency impact: extra per-request overhead introduced by condensation step. Target <10ms added for Dedicated; <25ms for Private/edge.
- Memory reduction: tokens or bytes saved in working set. Goal: 4–10x compaction with <5% quality loss for common queries.
- Rehydration cost: expected tokens to re-load when access misses; should be bounded.

Operational concerns:
- Determinism vs randomness: summaries with temperature can be non-deterministic; we need deterministic mode for caching and tracing.
- Auditability/compliance: summaries lose verbatim content — for regulated customers we need option to keep raw logs or reversible pointers.
- Model drift & regression monitoring: tie condensation to Redwood Optimize evals — run a prompt set to detect regressions.
- Storage & indexing: compacted artifacts need light indexing for retrieval; prefer embedding + small metadata for quick filter.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How often do users ask for verbatim replays vs high-level understanding? (customer data needed)
- Does compactification magnify hallucination risk because evidence is removed? Need targeted hallucination probes.
- Hybrid policy design: when to evict vs when to rehydrate automatically? (cost-sensitive policy)
- Interaction with KV cache: if we compact past tokens, can we still reuse KV cache keys? Probably need mapping layer.

Short-term plan (next 2 sprints):
- Sprint 1: implement A) heuristic entity-anchor extractor as a fast python shim in local runtime. Create simple offline eval harness using session corpus from CS sandbox (anonymized).
- Sprint 2: implement B) progressive summarizer as a service call pattern; instrument cost/latency and attach to per-route traces in Console. Also add a few regression evals in Optimize.

Notes to self:
- Ask Legal about retention rules for compressed summaries (May 2029).
- Check with Solutions Eng which customers have strict verbatim audit requirements; prioritize those in tests.
- Slack convo id saved in linked_artifacts above.

Reminders / TODOs:
- [ ] Build small offline corpus (50 sessions, 20–200 turns) anonymized.
- [ ] Implement quick precision/recall probes for entity/QA fidelity.
- [ ] Prototype simple embedding-centroid condense and measure index size.
- [ ] Draft short one-pager for product about tradeoffs (for internal review).

Random heuristics that performed OK in my toy runs:
- Keep last 256 tokens verbatim, then for older content keep only sentences containing: user questions, named entities, numeric facts, or system instructions.
- If summary length would exceed X, prefer anchors over full-sentence summaries.

Final thought: compactification feels like a multi-armed bandit — different apps care about different signals. We should ship a small set of deterministic, configurable policies (entity-anchor, summary-anchor, embedding-centroid) and measure which defaults work for common workloads. Then layer a lightweight tuner in Optimize to recommend policies per-customer.

End of scratchpad (save and iterate).
